Trade | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Trade Image Washington state is home to one of the largest export economies in the country with over 40% of jobs being supported by international trade—that means a voice for strong and supportive trade policies is critical.  As a Yakima Valley farmer, I understand how important our products are to the supply chain and how critical it is that our agriculture, manufacturing, and retail producers are well-positioned in the global economy. I am proud we play a leading role in the pursuit of obtaining energy independence. If the United States is to be at the forefront of energy production and innovation, our federal policy must take a page out of Central Washington’s book and aggressively pursue an “all-of-the-above” energy approach. As Chairman of the Western Caucus and a member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development , fighting to develop our domestic energy resources is of the utmost importance to me and I am committed to restoring energy independence and ensuring a stronger America for generations to come. Hanford | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Hanford Image In Central Washington, we are aware of the important role Hanford played in bringing an end to World War II and winning the Cold War. The federal government now has a legal and moral obligation to clean up the legacy of nuclear waste. Ensuring that Hanford has the resources and oversight required to continue cleanup progress and meet the federal government's legal cleanup commitments is my top priority. I have had the opportunity to get a first-hand look at the critical cleanup activities being accomplished at Hanford and this work must continue as safely, quickly, and efficiently as possible. I am a co-chair of the House Nuclear Cleanup Caucus, and meet regularly with Hanford officials and Tri City leaders to ensure Hanford's cleanup needs are being met. I am continually communicating with my colleagues in Congress and with the highest levels of the Administration to advocate for proper funding and federal policies that will allow us to meet the many cleanup challenges at Hanford. Success at Hanford depends on other factors as well, such as the availability for storing spent nuclear fuel at the Yucca Mountain Repository. I am focused on continuing to develop Yucca Mountain, which has already been identified as scientifically safe and remains the legal, Congressionally-mandated repository where much of Hanford's nuclear waste will eventually be sent for long-term storage. Wasting decades of work and billions of taxpayer dollars by disregarding this legal repository makes no sense and does nothing to get Hanford's nuclear waste out of our state sooner.   More on Hanford Op-ed: Federal government remains committed to Hanford cleanup June 16, 2026 Weekly Columns and Op-Eds During World War II, the Hanford Site played a pivotal role in propelling the United States to win the nuclear arms race, which put an end to combat in the Pacific Theater. Veterans | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Veterans Image The responsibility of keeping our great nation free and safe rests on the shoulders of the men and women bravely serving in our Armed Forces. The care we provide to our veterans reflects our gratitude to the courageous servicemen and women who have risked their lives in the pursuit of freedom and liberty. My time in Congress has been filled with work to better serve the thousands of veterans in Central Washington. I have introduced legislation to fix the VA’s handling of the Oracle Cerner electronic health record (EHR) system, promoted community engagement with Gold Star Families , and fought for easier access to claim files and GI bill reimbursements .  My annual Veterans Service Fair offers opportunities to explore available resources like healthcare benefits, counseling, and employment opportunities for those who have served. Education | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Education Image Across the nation, we are seeing a concerning rise in parents being kept out of the loop when decisions are made about their own children. Our schools are empowered to teach based on personal biases and opinions, neglecting to notify parents when children are struggling with various crises, sidestepping parental choice.  This cannot continue and is why I am taking the necessary steps to protect the students of Central Washington and encourage transparency in our system.  I was proud to sponsor and help pass H.R. 5, the Parents Bill of Rights Act , which would put practices in place to facilitate meaningful dialog between a family and their child's school and lead to more parental input throughout the learning process. I also supported H.R. 734, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act , to defend female athletes across the country, ensure we’re giving our women and girls a fair playing field, and keep biological males out of women’s sports. As the war in Israel rages on, I am committed to fighting the rise of antisemitism in our post-secondary schools and oppose the radical efforts to unfairly cancel student loan debt. I was also proud to combat the Administration’s efforts to prohibit school archery and hunting programs from receiving federal funding—a clear example of the federal government sticking its hand where it shouldn’t be. Wildfires and Forest Management | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Wildfires and Forest Management Image The catastrophic wildfires facing our region are, unfortunately, something we have come to expect during the dry, summer months, and I am committed to working with local officials to ensure we have the resources we need to prepare, prevent, and recover when the time comes.  I have seen firsthand how our communities have worked together to help one another during these natural disasters. Firefighters from across the U.S. have joined the fight and volunteers from all over the state and country provide support and relief to displaced residents. These men and women put their lives on the line to protect our homes, businesses, and communities throughout wildfire season. I introduced the Fair Pay for Federal Firefighters Act to deliver on my promise to our Central Washington heroes by enacting a short-term solution to prevent the United States Department of Agriculture from enacting scheduled pay cuts for our federal firefighters due to a lack of funds.  I have also been working diligently to ensure our farmers are not devastated by these disasters, which is why I introduced legislation to require the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation (FCIC) to carry out research and implement a crop insurance product that covers losses due to smoke exposure.   More on Wildfires and Forest Management ICYMI: Newhouse Holds Forestry and Horticulture Subcommittee Hearing with U.S. Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz July 22, 2026 Press Release Press Release   For Immediate Release: July 22, 2026 Contact: Juan Ayala, (202) 713-7750 WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, House Forestry and Horticulture Subcommittee Chairman Dan Newhouse (WA-04) held a hearing to receive an update about the U.S. Forest Service's priorities regarding wildfire management, disaster recovery, recreation access, and infrastructure.   Issues : Wildfires and Forest Management Image Newhouse Votes to Advance Farm Bill from Committee March 5, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Health Care | Congressman Dan Newhouse Skip to main content Health Care Image I was proud to vote to restore individual healthcare choices and government accountability by repealing Obamacare. I continue to hear personal stories from individuals in Central Washington about the uncertainty and dramatic cost increases Obamacare has created for their families and businesses. A top-down, mandate-centered, one-size-fits-all approach to healthcare does not work for families or businesses in Central Washington. Obamacare has caused health insurance premiums and increased deductibles to become less affordable for too many Americans, which is why I am working with my colleagues in Congress to ensure patient-centered care that will increase access and make insurance more affordable. Americans should have the freedom to purchase insurance across state lines, protection for patients with preexisting conditions, and care for our most vulnerable citizens.
